name: RoboBench
description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation across 5 dimensions, 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
citeAs: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang. ROBOBENCH: A COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION BENCHMARK FOR MULTIMODAL LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS AS EMBODIED BRAIN. arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: To evaluate five cognitive dimensions, the benchmark builds datasets from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Instruction comprehension uses paired explicit and implicit instructions, where explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions are rewritten from them using LLMs. Perception reasoning datasets are constructed across robotic-centric, object-centric, scene-centric, and task-centric aspects using real robot data, curated attributes, segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning is built from high-quality robotic videos by extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs. Affordance prediction samples representative frames from the planning pool and annotates static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis collects execution-level failures from RoboMIND and synthesizes planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data combine large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection. Planning data are built from high-quality robotic videos from sources including Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, and other cited robotic datasets; perception uses real robot data, curated static attributes, segmented video steps, and human-labeled bounding boxes; failure analysis uses execution-level failures from RoboMIND.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions, including wrong object, missing step, and wrong order. Explicit instructions are rewritten into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs. For planning, frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs and each step is mapped into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The benchmark applies both general and task-specific filters during construction. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. For planning, frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs from videos. Perception data are standardized into multiple-choice QA. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators conduct quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is used: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail undergo manual review and correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are provided by MLLMs and humans depending on the subtask. For planning, Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata such as objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments, which are then refined by human annotators. Perception uses template-based QA, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps for temporal grounding, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes for spatial and causal reasoning, and human-labeled bounding boxes linking instructions to target objects. Affordance prediction annotates representative frames with static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions. Failure analysis execution-level failures are labeled by experts. Human study expert annotators assigned holistic planning scores from 0 to 20.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper describes a two-stage quality control process with post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators and a majority-vote strategy. Items that all models solve correctly are removed, while items all models fail undergo manual review and correction. For planning metric validation, expert annotators assigned holistic scores from 0 to 20 and the authors compared human scores with automated approaches using Pearson correlation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections; expert annotators with prior training assigned holistic scores in the human study.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs, MLLMs, Gemini, GPT, VLMs, detection models
rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench is intended to provide a unified scaffold for measuring embodied cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing planning data primarily focus on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which may contribute to failures in dual-arm coordination and mobile manipulation. It also notes that models perform relatively better on common, well-seen objects and worse on uncommon objects, symbolic reasoning, or world knowledge.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reports that planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Human performance on execution-level failure diagnosis is relatively low, underscoring intrinsic task difficulty. The paper also highlights that current MLLMs exhibit major gaps in implicit instruction grounding, robot-view recognition, temporal grounding, cross-scenario planning, fine-grained affordance understanding, and execution failure diagnosis.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It is used for systematic evaluation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, including leaderboard-style comparison of state-of-the-art MLLMs and human reference evaluation.
